info.title: Monster Raid Service API
info.description:
Owns each guild's active cooperative raid, its participants, attacks, timer, monster health, and settlement result. An active raid uses a snapshot of the selected Package Registry configuration so that later configuration changes cannot alter a raid already in progress.

The service publishes the `raid.started.v1`, `raid.completed.v1`, and `raid.failed.v1` queue events. Event payload schemas are included under components for reference; events are delivered through the message queue using the common event envelope, not over HTTP.

The service runs as three interchangeable instances behind the gateway. Every response carries `X-Instance-Id`, and each instance registers itself with Service Discovery, which polls `/status`. Every peer call goes through a circuit breaker: three failures within 14 seconds open it for 14 seconds, then one trial call decides. Each peer has its own breaker, so Guild being down never stops calls to Tamagotchi. Crediting rewards through User Management keeps its existing deferred-settlement path while that circuit is open, and reading a raid or its result never needs a peer.

servers.description: Gateway; external callers send bearer tokens. Trusted headers are injected by the gateway.

503.description: GUILD_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: Guild Service could not be reached; PEER_CIRCUIT_OPEN: Guild failed three times within 14 seconds, so this instance did not call it (sent with Retry-After: 14); or CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_REACHED: the service is already handling as many requests as it admits (sent with Retry-After: 1)

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying: 14 for PEER_CIRCUIT_OPEN, 1 for CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_REACHED, absent otherwise

post.summary: Create a guild raid from an active schedule
post.description: Callable only by guild members. Creation is idempotent for the combination of guildId and scheduleId: if concurrent requests attempt to create the same guild raid, only one active instance is stored. Publishes `raid.started.v1` after the raid is created.

503.description: GUILD_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE or PACKAGE_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE: Guild or Package Registry could not be reached; PEER_CIRCUIT_OPEN: Guild or Package Registry failed three times within 14 seconds, so this instance did not call it (sent with Retry-After: 14); or CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_REACHED: the service is already handling as many requests as it admits (sent with Retry-After: 1)

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying: 14 for PEER_CIRCUIT_OPEN, 1 for CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_REACHED, absent otherwise

get.description: Callable only by members of the guild that owns the raid.

post.description: Callable only by guild members. Joining requires an active Guild Service membership and ownership of the submitted primary Tamagotchi.

get.description: Callable only by members of the guild that owns the raid.

post.description: Callable only by raid participants. Damage is calculated server side from the attacking Tamagotchi combat profile and the raid configuration snapshot; client-provided damage values are never trusted. Attacks are rate limited per participant. Deduplicated by the client-generated actionId.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying: 14 for PEER_CIRCUIT_OPEN, 1 for CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_REACHED, absent otherwise

servers.description: Service root on the internal network, outside /api/v1; not exposed through the API Gateway

get.description: Answers `200 {"status":"UP"}` whenever the process serves HTTP and checks nothing else, PostgreSQL or Redis included. A liveness probe that checked dependencies would restart every instance at once when a shared dependency failed, and a restart cannot bring the dependency back. Docker's healthcheck calls it. It needs no identity, bypasses the concurrency limit and is never cached.

servers.description: Service root on the internal network, outside /api/v1; not exposed through the API Gateway

get.description: Polled directly by Service Discovery every 4 seconds to decide whether this instance receives traffic. The status is the first rule that matches: PostgreSQL or Redis unreachable gives `DOWN` with `503`; utilization at or above 0.8, or a peer `DOWN` or its circuit open, gives `DEGRADED` with `200`; otherwise `UP` with `200`. Neither load nor a failing peer ever produces `DOWN`. Each datastore probe has its own one second deadline, the probes run concurrently and the result is reused for one second. Peers are never probed: their entries come from this instance's circuit breakers, `DOWN` while the circuit is open. It needs no identity, bypasses the concurrency limit and answers while every permit is taken.

503.description: `DOWN`: PostgreSQL or Redis is unreachable, so nothing can be served

CorrelationId.description: Traces one operation across services and events; generated by the gateway when absent

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Deduplicates retriable commands that create side effects

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous page

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of items per page

X-Caller-Kind.name: X-Caller-Kind
X-Caller-Kind.description: Caller kind set by the gateway on every forwarded request: user, service or anonymous. Never accepted from an external client; a request that reaches the service without it is rejected with 401.

X-User-ID.name: X-User-ID
X-User-ID.description: Authenticated user UUID, set for user callers. Ownership and membership checks compare this value with the path parameter, never the reverse.

X-Session-ID.name: X-Session-ID
X-Session-ID.description: Session UUID for user callers, when the token carries one.

X-Service-Name.name: X-Service-Name
X-Service-Name.description: Authenticated service name, set for service callers.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or malformed gateway identity: MISSING_IDENTITY or INVALID_IDENTITY. The gateway is the only source of the identity headers, so a request arriving without them fails closed rather than being guessed at.

ServiceUnavailable.description: CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_REACHED: the service is already handling as many requests as it admits and rejects the request at once instead of queueing it

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier of the failed operation

CombatType.description: Combat type used for weakness and resistance calculations

scheduleId.description: Active Package Registry schedule used to initialize the raid
Schedule from which the raid was created

status.description: Current raid lifecycle state. When monster HP reaches zero the raid enters SETTLING and performs idempotent reward commands keyed by raidId; it becomes COMPLETED only after all required reward commands succeed. If the deadline arrives while monster HP is above zero, the raid becomes FAILED and no rewards are distributed

endsAt.description: Deadline copied from the active schedule

name.description: Monster name copied from the configuration

performedAt.description: Client-observed attack time used for validation

status.description: Whether the monster was defeated before the deadline

rewards.description: Per-participant rewards; empty for a failed raid

finishedAt.description: Time at which the terminal state was reached

globalCurrency.description: Currency credited through User Management Service

EventEnvelope.description: Common envelope for every event sent through the message queue. Not delivered over HTTP.

eventId.description: Unique event identifier used for deduplication

eventType.description: Stable event name including the version suffix

occurredAt.description: Time at which the business event occurred

correlationId.description: Identifier connecting the event to the originating operation

RaidStartedEventV1.description: Payload of `raid.started.v1`, published after a guild raid is created. Notification Service consumes it to notify guild members.

RaidFinishedEventV1.description: Shared payload of `raid.completed.v1` and `raid.failed.v1`, published only after the corresponding terminal state is stored. Notification Service consumes both to notify guild members and participants.

finishedAt.description: Time at which the terminal state was stored

service.description: Canonical service name, the route key in the gateway configuration

instanceId.description: Hostname of this instance, the same value as X-Instance-Id

uptimeSeconds.description: Whole seconds since the instance started serving

checkedAt.description: UTC with milliseconds and a Z suffix

inFlight.description: Requests currently held by the concurrency limiter

utilization.description: inFlight / limit rounded to two decimals, 0.0 when the limit is 0

circuit.description: Peers only: the state of this instance's circuit breaker for that peer. A half-open circuit is reported as OPEN

InstanceId.description: Hostname of the instance that answered. Every response carries it, errors included, so a caller can tell the instances apart
